section_summary: This section documents the mounting difficulties faced by American motion picture companies operating in Japan during 1941, focusing on foreign exchange restrictions, blocked assets, and tightened governmental control. It details controversies surrounding Paramount Pictures' purchase of Japanese Government bonds to release frozen yen, proposals to transfer blocked funds to the Mitsui Trust Company, and an informal Japanese diplomatic protest against the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer film 'They Met in Bombay' (initially 'The Uniform'). The later documents follow escalating labor tensions in Tokyo as Japanese employees demanded substantial dismissal and retirement allowances amid severe box office restrictions and impending liquidation, culminating in a police-mediated settlement accepted by American parent companies.

subfiles.about: A letter clarifying the State Department's strong disapproval of American motion picture companies investing blocked funds in Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Hamilton tells Carl Milliken, citing Paramount's John Hicks's letter on Japanese bonds, that Grew had warned film representatives; Japan's resources serve policies prejudicial to American interests, and buying bonds aids them and encourages Japan to keep blocking American funds.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to Carl E. Milliken regarding Paramount's Purchase of Japanese Bonds
subfiles.to: Carl E. Milliken, Acting Foreign Manager, Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America, Inc.

subfiles.about: An instruction transmitting correspondence and a memorandum of conversation concerning Paramount's investment in Japanese national bonds.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction 2182 sends Grew, in confidence, Milliken's March 26, 1941 letter, the Department's April 2 reply and a May 21 conversation memorandum on Paramount's Tokyo representative buying Japanese national bonds.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 2182 to the American Ambassador at Tokyo regarding Investment in Japanese National Bonds
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: An internal memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 5462 on Japanese bond purchases and a deposit offer from Mitsui Trust Company.
subfiles.from: Schmidt, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Summary of Despatch 5462: Paramount's Jonas Albeck ordered Japanese bonds on J. E. Perkins's instructions despite Embassy warnings; Mitsui Trust offered Warner Brothers' manager five-year deposits of frozen film funds with interest and withdrawal provisions.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 5462: Purchase of Japanese National Bonds by American Motion Picture Concerns
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: A despatch detailing Paramount's purchase of Japanese Government bonds and a banking deposit proposal from the Mitsui Trust Company.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Paramount Films Ltd. purchased 765,000 yen of Japanese Government bonds after receiving approval from New York, despite warnings that it aided Japan's war program and endangered other American assets. Paramount secured permission to remit ten percent of the principal and annual interest to the United States, plus a repurchase agreement from the Finance Minister. The despatch also details an alternative proposal from the Mitsui Trust Company to hold approximately eight million yen in frozen film funds on deposit at interest.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5462 from Tokyo: Purchase of Japanese National Bonds by American Motion Picture Concerns

subfiles.about: A brief letter acknowledging receipt of the Department's views on Paramount's bond purchases.
subfiles.from: Carl E. Milliken, Acting Foreign Manager, Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Milliken thanks Hamilton for the April 2 letter on Paramount's Japanese bonds and is passing it to John Hicks.
subfiles.title: Letter from Carl E. Milliken to Maxwell M. Hamilton regarding Japanese Bonds
subfiles.to: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A comprehensive quarterly economic and consular report on the motion picture industry and regulations in Japan.
subfiles.from: Donald W. Lamm, American Vice Consul, and Frank S. Williams, Commercial Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This report reviews the major developments affecting the Japanese film market during the first quarter of 1941. It covers reductions in raw film allotments, reorganization of distribution under 'new structure' national policies, and the promotion of domestic cultural and propaganda films abroad. It also provides 1940 statistics on theatre attendance and film censorship, describes the creation of an actors' school, details new technical inventions by Japanese mechanics, and notes the propaganda mission of S. Taguchi to the United States.
subfiles.title: Report No. 167: Motion Picture Developments in Japan Proper, First Quarter - 1941

subfiles.about: A charge slip recording the borrowing of an enclosure from file 894.4061.
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records clerk mb
subfiles.summary: Charge slip: an enclosure from file 894.4061 charged to Frank S. Williams on January 6, 1944.
subfiles.title: Charge Slip for Enclosure to File 894.4061 Charged to Frank S. Williams

subfiles.about: Handwritten notes analyzing the advantages and policy implications of depositing film funds with the Mitsui Trust Company.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, and Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.summary: Walter A. Adams notes that while Mitsui would benefit as a banker by holding the funds, National City Bank desires to withdraw from Japan and Mitsui offers film companies interest and withdrawal privileges. Stanley K. Hornbeck initials and concludes that the Department cannot object to the proposed arrangement.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Walter A. Adams and Stanley K. Hornbeck on Mitsui Trust Company Deposit

subfiles.about: A handwritten reference note recording contact information for Carl E. Milliken.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Note giving Carl Milliken's name, address (28 West 44th Street, New York) and title, Acting Foreign Manager of the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America.
subfiles.title: Note on Carl E. Milliken of Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America

subfiles.about: An economic evaluation of the Mitsui Trust Company deposit proposal for blocked American film revenues.
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Economic Adviser says the Mitsui deposit plan doesn't conflict with the policy against loans to Japan if withdrawals follow Finance Ministry exchange permits; blocked funds are an involuntary credit anyway, and keeping them liquid is the best compromise.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Adviser on International Economic Affairs to Stanley K. Hornbeck regarding Mitsui Deposit Proposal
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: A brief handwritten comment regarding the Economic Affairs memorandum on the Mitsui proposal.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note from the Adviser on Political Relations referring to the Economic Adviser's views on the film funds deposit.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Note from Adviser on Political Relations regarding Economic Affairs Memo

subfiles.about: A memorandum recording Carl E. Milliken's inquiry into the Department's views on the Mitsui Trust Company proposal.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams and Schmidt, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Milliken informally seeks views on Mitsui Trust's offer to take blocked film funds on deposit; Walter Adams personally sees no objection and will consult colleagues if others differ.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Carl E. Milliken, Walter A. Adams, and Mr. Schmidt regarding Mitsui Deposit

subfiles.about: An instruction transmitting the memorandum of conversation of May 6, 1941 with Carl E. Milliken.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Instruction 2178 sends Grew the May 6, 1941 memorandum of Milliken's talk with State officers on depositing frozen film funds with Mitsui Trust.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 2178 to the American Ambassador at Tokyo regarding Mitsui Deposit Proposal
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: A memorandum recommending that Ambassador Grew's letter to Will H. Hays regarding 'They Met in Bombay' be withheld.
subfiles.from: Schmidt, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: MGM confirmed "The Uniform" was released nationwide as "They Met in Bombay"; Schmidt recommends withholding Grew's letter to Will Hays and telling General Milliken informally.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 5660: Film 'They Met in Bombay'
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and officers of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A memorandum confirming the Department's consensus to brief Governor Milliken informally rather than deliver Grew's letter to Hays.
subfiles.from: Joseph Keating, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Keating tells Wolf Grew's draft letter on the Japanese complaint against MGM's "The Uniform" wasn't delivered to Hays; the consensus is to inform Milliken informally, as it now plays as "They Met in Bombay."
subfiles.title: Memorandum from J. Keating to Mr. Wolf regarding 'The Uniform' ('They Met in Bombay')
subfiles.to: Mr. Wolf, Division of International Communications

subfiles.about: A routing memorandum submitting Tokyo Despatch No. 5660 and its enclosed letter to Hays for review.
subfiles.from: Schmidt, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Schmidt submits Despatch 5660 with Grew's letter to Will Hays and Cooper's Foreign Office conversation memorandum, so officers can decide whether to forward the letter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo Despatch No. 5660 on Japanese Complaint Against MGM Film
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck and Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch forwarding a proposed letter to Will H. Hays and a memorandum of conversation regarding Japanese Foreign Office objections to an American motion picture.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits for Department discretion a letter addressed to Will H. Hays, President of MPPDA, concerning complaints raised by the Japanese Foreign Office against the MGM film 'The Uniform' (later released as 'They Met in Bombay'). Grew's letter explains that while reports of Japanese wartime atrocities are widespread abroad, portraying Japanese soldiers attempting to violate Chinese women causes intense resentment in Japan and inflames public opinion. The accompanying memorandum by Third Secretary Charles A. Cooper records a June 5 conference with S. Yuki of the Japanese Foreign Office, who requested the scene be deleted or publicity suppressed, also noting objection to Universal's 'Half Way to Shanghai'. Both file copies and unmailed originals of the enclosures are included.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5660 from Tokyo: Informal Complaint by Japanese Foreign Office Against 'The Uniform' (with Enclosures)

subfiles.about: An instruction informing Ambassador Grew that his letter to Will H. Hays will not be forwarded because the film is already released.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Welles acknowledges Despatch 5660 on the Japanese complaint against "The Uniform"; the film already played as "They Met in Bombay," so State will inform the Hays organization informally, not forward the letter.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 2205 to the American Ambassador at Tokyo regarding 'They Met in Bombay'
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting tightening financial and censorship restrictions in Japan and radical employee demands against Universal Pictures.
subfiles.from: American Motion Picture Association of Tokyo (via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew)
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1193: Tokyo film association says Japan refused expenditure and deposit permits, requires Censor Board scrutiny of prints and controls bookings and prices; Universal's Japanese staff demand 55 percent of stock, a 30 percent raise and immunity from dismissal.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1193 from Tokyo transmitting AMPA Message to Frederick L. Herron
subfiles.to: Frederick L. Herron, Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America (via Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: A telegram transmitting a request from the Hays office for details on the Universal staff dispute.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Telegram 499: Hull tells Tokyo the Hays office is meeting film companies on Japan difficulties and asks manager Perkins to cable full details on employees' claims and settlement.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 499 to the American Embassy at Tokyo regarding Universal Employee Claims

subfiles.about: A telegraphic request that the State Department ask its Tokyo mission for details on Universal's staff dispute.
subfiles.from: Carl E. Milliken, Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America
subfiles.summary: Milliken thanks Keating, says executives meet Thursday, and asks the Department to cable Tokyo for Universal manager Perkins's details on employee demands and settlement efforts.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Carl E. Milliken to Joseph Keating requesting Cable to Universal Manager
subfiles.to: Joseph Keating, Division of International Communications, Department of State

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting the retraction of radical employee demands, new unified severance claims by sales managers, and severe booking bans.
subfiles.from: James E. Perkins (via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew)
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1276: Perkins says Universal staff dropped stock and board demands, but eight sales managers want two years' salary plus three months per year of service under police pressure; Japan banned about 80 percent of September bookings.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1276 from Tokyo transmitting Perkins' Report to J. H. Seidelman on Employee Demands
subfiles.to: J. H. Seidelman, Universal Pictures, New York (via Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: A telegram describing the collapse of film earnings due to censorship bans, staff reorganizations, and preparations for departure.
subfiles.from: Michael Shathin (via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew)
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1294: Michael Shathin reports 21 of 38 September pictures disapproved, leaving revenue at 1,100 yen monthly; he plans to leave operations to local staff, warns of lost control if diplomatic relations break, and needs a departure permit.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1294 from Tokyo transmitting Michael Shathin's Report to Warner Brothers
subfiles.to: Warner Brothers Pictures, New York (via Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: A letter detailing Paramount's Japanese Government bond transactions and requesting permission to fulfill its remaining commitment.
subfiles.from: James E. Perkins, General Manager in the Far East, Paramount Pictures Inc.
subfiles.summary: Perkins says Paramount agreed to buy 1,400,000 yen in Japanese bonds to release blocked revenues, 750,000 yen bought with ten percent remittable in dollars; committed before State's objections, he asks State not to disfavor completing the remaining 650,000 yen.
subfiles.title: Letter from James E. Perkins to Cordell Hull regarding Paramount's Bond Commitments
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State (Attention Walter A. Adams)

subfiles.about: A formal acknowledgment of Perkins' explanatory letter regarding Paramount's bond purchases.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams, Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Adams acknowledges Perkins's May 23, 1941 letter on Paramount's Japanese bond purchases, now in the official records.
subfiles.title: Letter from Walter A. Adams to James E. Perkins acknowledging Statement on Bond Purchases
subfiles.to: James E. Perkins, Paramount Pictures, Incorporated

subfiles.about: A memorandum recording a telephone call from Carl E. Milliken arranging an appointment for James E. Perkins.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams, Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Carl E. Milliken telephoned the Department to arrange an interview for James E. Perkins, who had returned from Japan and wished to explain Paramount's purchase of Japanese Government bonds. Adams scheduled an appointment for Perkins to visit his office on May 21.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Carl E. Milliken and Walter A. Adams on James E. Perkins' Visit

subfiles.about: A conference memorandum recording Paramount officials' explanation of their Japanese bond purchases and commitments.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville and Walter A. Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Perkins and Mr. Clement tell Adams and Coville Paramount committed to 1,400,000 yen of Japanese bonds before learning of State's objections, with 10 percent dollar remittance and 3.5 percent interest transfer, profits accruing 100,000 yen monthly; they pledge no further bonds.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with James E. Perkins and Mr. Clement on Paramount's Bond Purchases

subfiles.about: A telegram inquiring about terms and advisability of a proposed compromise settlement with Japanese film employees.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Telegram 567: at Milliken's request Hull asks Tokyo for the terms of a proposed compromise settlement between American film distributors' Tokyo offices and local employees and Grew's views before Tuesday's deadline.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 567 to the American Embassy at Tokyo regarding Proposed Employee Settlement

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting the six terms of an employee retirement and dismissal agreement negotiated through Tokyo police mediation.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1421: Grew details police-mediated terms: a month's pay per year up to five years, 1.5 months beyond, with safeguards and discretionary bonuses; he urges parent companies to accept before Tuesday.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1421 from Tokyo regarding Police-Mediated Employee Settlement Terms

subfiles.about: A telegram transmitting six counter-conditions from American film companies concerning the employee agreement.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Telegram 589: Hull relays the film companies' counterproposals, including the right to liquidate, release of frozen funds if indemnities exceed earnings, half indemnities for voluntary resignations, segregated funds and a two-year limit, for the Film Board.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 589 to the American Embassy at Tokyo transmitting Film Companies' Counterproposals

subfiles.about: A telegram communicating the final unified dismissal and resignation agreement accepted by AMPA and answering parent-company queries.
subfiles.from: American Motion Picture Association of Tokyo (via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew)
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1484: the association reports the final severance schedule accepted: a month per year up to five years, 1.5 after, half for voluntary resignations; liquidation needs Home Ministry approval, frozen funds may pay indemnities, police rejected a time limit, and import permits stay separate.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1484 from Tokyo transmitting Final Employee Agreement Adopted by AMPA

subfiles.about: A telegram confirming unanimous parent-company approval of the Tokyo employee agreement.
subfiles.from: Cordell Hull, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Telegram 609: Hull relays the Hays organization's message that American film companies unanimously accept the employee settlement in Tokyo's telegram 1484.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 609 to the American Embassy at Tokyo transmitting Acceptance of Employee Settlement

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch reporting official representations made to the Japanese Foreign Office against exorbitant staff demands.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch 5824: on August 29 Grew protests at the Foreign Office against exorbitant demands by Japanese employees on American film firms, which face closure and a possible state film monopoly, and requests intervention.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5824 from Tokyo: Representations Regarding Demands Made upon American Motion Picture Companies
